title: Alternating ZnSe/ZnS 16-layer stack on Ge with expanded thickness bounds for dual-band IR filtering
scientific_hypothesis: An alternating ZnSe/ZnS multilayer with individually optimized thicknesses can simultaneously achieve high transmittance in 8000-11000 nm and suppressed transmittance in 3000-5000 nm on a Ge substrate, with performance improving as thickness bounds encompass the 784-1482 nm range observed in prior successful iterations.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics principle: alternating high/low refractive index layers create constructive/destructive interference patterns. Quarter-wave optical thickness at a design wavelength produces maximum reflectance at that wavelength; deviating from quarter-wave shifts the stopband position. By optimizing individual layer thicknesses rather than fixing them to quarter-wave, the stopband can be positioned at 3000-5000 nm while maintaining passband transmission at 8000-11000 nm.
proposed_topology: air | ZnSe(1) | ZnS(2) | ZnSe(3) | ZnS(4) | ZnSe(5) | ZnS(6) | ZnSe(7) | ZnS(8) | ZnSe(9) | ZnS(10) | ZnSe(11) | ZnS(12) | ZnSe(13) | ZnS(14) | ZnSe(15) | ZnS(16) | Ge
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 16 layers, each bounded 500-2000 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain physical validity (positive thickness, no absorption violations)
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness range 500-2000 nm is physically depositable by thermal evaporation or sputtering
Alternating sequence simplifies process control compared to aperiodic sequences
theory_basis: Recalled: Alternating high/low index dielectric stacks create wavelength-selective interference
Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce stopbands centered at design wavelength; thickness deviation shifts band position
Recalled: ZnSe has higher refractive index than ZnS in IR, providing index contrast for interference effects
Recalled: Ge substrate is transparent in LWIR but has high index requiring matching considerations
Recalled: 16 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization without excessive complexity
expected_advantages: Expanded thickness bounds (500-2000 nm vs prior 150-600 nm) better encompass the 784-1482 nm range from iteration_08 which achieved highest target_score
Fixed alternating topology reduces search space complexity compared to optimizing layer sequence
Individual thickness optimization allows fine-tuning of stopband position beyond simple quarter-wave design
known_risks: ZnSe material name 'znse' is not in guaranteed_names list; local resolution must succeed or route fails - this settled by checking material_catalog.measured_not_tunable guidance that other names are allowed if resolvable
Recalled refractive index contrast between ZnSe and ZnS in 3000-11000 nm range is approximate; actual n/k data from registry will determine achievable performance
Quarter-wave design intuition at these long wavelengths may not translate directly; optimal thicknesses may differ significantly from λ/4n estimates
Thermal expansion mismatch between ZnSe/ZnS and Ge could cause stress in cryogenic operation, but this is outside TMM scope
Did not verify whether 500-2000 nm bounds are optimal; may need further expansion if optimizer hits bounds repeatedly
execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer planar dielectric stack on Ge substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS, ZnSe (Querry), ZnS (alternating, starting with ZnSe (Querry)). Each layer thickness is an independent optimization variable bounded between 500 nm and 2000 nm. Wavelength range: 3000-11000 nm. Target behavior: maximize transmittance in 8000-11000 nm band, minimize transmittance in 3000-5000 nm band. Use coherent transfer matrix method solver. Normal incidence. Unpolarized or TE polarization. Materials resolved from registry: ZnSe (Querry), zns, ge.
revision_reason: Continuation of control route with expanded thickness bounds (500-2000 nm vs prior 150-600 nm) to better encompass the 784-1482 nm thickness range from iteration_08 which achieved the highest target_score (0.363) among completed runs. Topology and material choices unchanged to isolate thickness bound effect.
